main_result.conversion: On an open seven-dimensional product region, an actual ProductCoordinateWeakHk family yields ProductMixedMultiIndexWeakHk at the same finite order and same per-derivative squared L2 budget.
main_result.indices: Alpha : Fin 4 -> Nat counts the four Y coordinate derivatives; beta : Fin 3 -> Nat counts the three T coordinate derivatives. The sum of their entries is the actual coordinate word length.
main_result.witness: F(alpha,beta) = D(mixedMultiIndexWord alpha beta), with F(0,0)=f, genuine region L2 membership through total order m, and bundled Y/T weak derivative identities to F(alpha+single_i(1),beta) and F(alpha,beta+single_j(1)) below total order m.
main_result.raw_corollary: For c>0, local smooth real B and local smooth arbitrary complex s, a raw locally L2 complex solution of the sole compact-test equation (-Delta_Y-c*norm(Y)^2*Delta_T+B)f=s has this finite natural-multiindex family on every supplied strictly nested positive-width box whose outer closed box lies in the open domain.
main_result.quantifiers: For every finite m there exist W>=0 and a family F. The result does not quantify a single common all-order family or order-independent W.

checks: The canonical word is inherited from the pre-existing Fin 7 representation. The new mixedMultiIndex is the exact pullback of Sum.elim alpha beta along sevenCoordinateEquiv, with proved separate Y/T counts and exact total length. No coordinate multiplicity is discarded.

Each canonical single-coordinate shift is proved by equality of literal list element counts. The shift theorem orientation is shifted canonical word Perm prefixed old canonical word; the final derivative proof correctly uses its symmetry.

The permutation proof commutes only smooth test derivatives. Their transposed recursive word convention is respected in the nil, cons and adjacent-swap steps. Permutation preserves word length, so the (-1)^length weak integration-by-parts sign remains unchanged.

Actual region L2 budgets establish local integrability of the difference of representatives and integrability of both compact test products before integral_sub. Equality against all smooth compact tests then gives local almost-everywhere equality on an open domain.

The final derivative transfer uses congr_ae_local with the first representative unchanged and the derivative representative replaced by the locally AE-equal canonical shifted word. No pointwise equality or pointwise mixed-derivative commutation is asserted.

The strict old-order bound total<m is exactly sufficient to access the prefixed derivative word at length<=m. There is no request for a derivative at m+1. Every natural multiindex of total order<=m receives the same inherited per-word budget.
At m=0, the zero-index canonical word is empty, and the weak derivative shift premises are false. The output is the original L2-only zero-order package, not an unsupported differentiability claim.

The raw local PDE corollary supplies the open inner box and invokes the already reviewed raw finite regularity theorem. No source-chain, solution-derivative, positive-order PDE or cutoff-stage premise has been added to its final hypotheses.
scope_limits: These files provide genuine ordinary natural-multiindex weak derivative identities in the explicitly defined predicate. They do not prove an equivalence to a separate Mathlib or conventional packaged Sobolev space.
W bounds each squared derivative norm separately. A summed Hm norm would require an additional finite-count factor or separate aggregate theorem; it is not bounded by W in these statements.

No common all-order representative family, Sobolev embedding, smooth representative, factorial or analytic estimate, explicit rate, spectral conclusion, executable solver or complexity claim is established by this conversion.

The conversion is seven-dimensional (four Y and three T coordinates). The supporting permutation theorem is generic in finite spectator index, but the canonical mixed multiindices and final raw corollary are Fin 3.
